title: Data Sharing, Governance and Board Reporting
summary: Brings the programme together into a fraud governance framework: intelligence and data sharing, collaboration with other firms and law enforcement, management information and board oversight.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together into a fraud governance framework: intelligence and data sharing, collaboration with other firms and law enforcement, management information and board oversight.
Learning Objectives: Use intelligence and data sharing lawfully and effectively
Specify fraud management information and key risk indicators for the board
Produce an action plan to strengthen the firm's fraud framework
Syllabus: Data sharing between firms, industry bodies, telecoms, platforms and law enforcement
Recovering funds, mule account disruption and suspicious activity reporting
Fraud management information, loss metrics and board reporting
Workshop: fraud framework gap analysis and action plan
Intended Audience: Fraud prevention, fraud operations and investigations teams
Payments operations, customer service and complaints staff who handle suspected fraud cases
Compliance, financial crime and risk staff, and managers accountable for fraud outcomes
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of fraud, payments operations or financial crime compliance is helpful. No technical background in data analytics is required.
Core Reading: FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
G20/OECD High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection (2022)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)
